data.one_liner: iOS Liquid Glass widgets with Material 3 fallbacks on Android behind one adaptive API
data.what_it_does: Provides iOS Liquid Glass widgets matched to SwiftUI alongside Material 3 fallbacks for Android. It renders native SwiftUI glass on iOS 26+ and fragment shaders or Material surfaces elsewhere.
use_when: You want an iOS 26 Liquid Glass aesthetic that matches SwiftUI
You need platform-adaptive UI components (glass on iOS, Material 3 on Android) through a single API
You are building custom buttons, tab bars, sheets, and sliders with frosted glass effects
avoid_when: Your app strictly requires a traditional Material or Cupertino look without glassmorphism
You are targeting devices with very limited GPU memory where full-screen offscreen shader textures would be an issue
strengths: Pixel-identical to SwiftUI on iOS 26+ via native views
Cross-platform adaptive API with automatic Material 3 fallbacks on Android
Extensive preset library and fluid glass grouping/merging features
weaknesses: Shader glass can consume significant GPU memory on Android under Impeller
Requires iOS 26+ for native SwiftUI views, falling back to shaders on older versions
data.setup_notes: No Gradle dependencies or permissions required for the core UI, though shaders can optionally be preloaded via AdaptiveLiquidGlass.initialize().

alternatives.name: material_ui
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose this if you want a pure Material Design look instead of iOS-style liquid glass.

alternatives.name: cupertino_ui
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose this if you prefer standard native Apple Cupertino widgets instead of custom glass effects.
